title: Observability Gap Hypotheses and Run-Cards — cross-team rapid experiments
content:
Context and purpose:

This doc is a working scratchpad for short, cross-functional experiments aimed at closing high-impact observability gaps that are blocking SLO adoption and reliable incident triage for model-serving services. Primary goals: surface concrete hypotheses we can test in 1–3 sprints, produce lightweight run-cards + telemetry changes, and surface decisions for product/platform tradeoffs.

Audience: SREs, platform engineers, serving runtime, product-hosted-api, and solutions-eng.

Why this is different: many previous artifacts are roadmaps/playbooks. This is intentionally experimental and hypothesis-driven: each entry below is a small, scoped probe with a clear measurement plan and an exit criterion.

Top-level objectives (success criteria):
- Reduce time-to-detection for model-serving latency regressions by 30% for top 10% traffic services (measure: median detection lag from anomaly signal to alert).
- Increase fidelity of error-class attribution for user-facing failures (goal: actionable attribution 80% -> 95% on sampled incidents).
- De-risk SLO adoption by providing two reusable telemetry patterns (prefix-caching hit-rate and KV-cache saturation) and proving they work across 3 services.

Experiment catalog (pick 1–2 per sprint):
1) Prefix-cache telemetry probe (owner: Priya)
- Hypothesis: adding per-prefix cache hit metrics + 95th/99th percentile per-prefix latency will allow faster root-cause for cache-eviction-related regressions.
- Instrumentation: emit metric: prefix_cache.hits/<model_family>/<prefix_bucket>, prefix_cache.latency_ms.p95/p99; add tracing tag: cache_miss_reason.
- Success metric: reduction in time-to-attribution for cache-related incidents by 40% in the pilot services.
- Exit criteria: either metrics provide signal AND are low-cardinality; or they create too much cardinality -> roll back.
- Estimated effort: 3 engineer days + 1 SRE day for dashboards/alerts.
- Linked tickets: SERV-342 (prio), GH-obs-17.

2) Adaptive latency anomaly buckets (owner: Diego)
- Hypothesis: switching from static global latency thresholds to dynamic, workload-aware thresholds (per-model-version percentiles) will reduce false positives and focus on real regressions.
- Implementation: a small service that computes rolling 30-min p95 per route/model and feeds alerting engine; fallback to global thresholds.
- Success metric: 50% drop in false positive alerts for latency; maintain sensitivity for real incidents.
- Risk: increased complexity in alert routing; need to ensure we don’t miss outages during cold start of model variants.

3) Error-class enrichment pipeline (owner: Ethan)
- Hypothesis: parsing the first 3 frames of model-serving errors and mapping them to error-class taxonomy (network/db/kv-cache/model-oom/fallback) increases actionable attribution.
- Work: lightweight instrumenter (server-side) that attaches error_class label and provenance to traces and incidents.
- Success metric: increase in incidents with error_class populated from 80% -> 95% in trial group.

4) Canary SLO shadowing (owner: Maya)
- Hypothesis: running SLO checks in shadow mode (no page) for 30 days will surface configuration drift and false-positive gaps before turning them on.
- Setup: select 3 services with different traffic patterns, run SLO engine with shadow=true, store alerts in per-customer dashboard only.
- Success metric: number of actionable config changes identified and resolved during shadow phase (target >= 5 across 3 services).

Run-card templates (quick incident triage cheatsheets) — lightweight, 1-pagers we can graft into oncall rotation
- Run-card: Latency spike (model-serving)
  - Quick checks (2 min): check model variant rollout metric, recent kernel/infra deploys (past 30m), prefix-cache hit rate, burst queue length.
  - Quick fixes (5–20 min): if prefix-cache drop -> warm critical prefixes (manual replay); if variant rollout -> abort canary; if infra -> roll forward to last green capacity pool.
  - Escalation: if user-impacted requests > 5% and can’t be mitigated within 20m -> page platform eng.

- Run-card: High 5xx rate on hosted-api
  - Quick checks: error_class in traces, db connection error spikes, backend latency vs frontend ingress.
  - Workaround: enable degraded response (short-circuit non-critical augmentations) per route.

Measurement plan / signal definitions
- Detection lag: time from first anomalous metric point to an SRE-visible alert (tracked in incident metadata).
- Attribution fidelity: fraction of incidents with error_class assigned and accepted by responder as correct.
- Telemetry cost: estimated storage/ingest delta per metric change (budget threshold: +15% ingest allowed per pilot).

Cross-functional commitments and coordination
- Weekly 30m sync (Mon 10:00) — quick status, blockers. Owners: Priya + Diego.
- Slack channel: #sre-observability-experiments (create if missing).
- Monthly demo: present pilot dashboards in reliability guild meeting.

Decision gates and governance
- Gate 1 (end of pilot sprint): decide either to (A) promote telemetry + alerts to prod, (B) revise metrics and re-run pilot, or (C) abandon if ingest/cost or high-cardinality issues.
- Gate 2 (after 3 pilots): decide whether to bake patterns into an observability library and add to onboarding docs.

Risks, mitigations, and guardrails
- High cardinality metrics -> mitigation: restrict to top-K prefixes by traffic and aggregate remainder into an "other" bucket.
- Storage/ingest budget exceeded -> mitigation: sample traces (1% -> 10%) and use histogram aggregation instead of high-cardinality counters.
- False sense of coverage from canned run-cards -> mitigation: pair-run first 2 oncalls with SRE coach.

Implementation backlog (short list)
- Instrument prefix-cache metrics + initial dashboard (Priya, due: 2026-02-05)
- Implement dynamic latency threshold service prototype (Diego, spike due: 2026-02-19)
- Error-class enrichment middleware PR (Ethan, due: 2026-02-12)
- Shadow SLO run for three services (Maya + product-hosted-api contact), start: 2026-02-01, review: 2026-03-03

Meetings / notes (raw)
- 2026-01-14 kickoff: alignment on scopes. Action: Priya to draft metric naming convention (done).
- 2026-01-21 sync: Diego raised concern on alert churn; agreed to implement shadowing for 2 weeks.
- 2026-02-02 ad-hoc: Ethan demoed error-class parsing PoC; sampling stable at 2% overhead.

Open questions / TODOs
- Who signs off on telemetry cost vs product ROI for hosted customers? (Finance + Product). TODO: assign stakeholder.
- Where should enriched error_class be stored? traces only or events store as well? (tradeoff: trace retention cost vs event indexing usefulness).
- Decide canonical prefix bucketing strategy (length vs semantic) — follow-up workshop.

Quick wins (can do in <5d)
- Add cache_miss_reason tag to existing traces (SRE + runtime: 2d).
- Shadow SLO check for one low-traffic service to validate rule syntax (1d).
- Add a tiny dashboard showing p95 latency by model-version for top 10 endpoints (3d).

Communication plan
- Publish weekly status note to reliability guild digest and #sre-observability-experiments.
- Capture lessons learned as short templates and add to shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/experiments/ (post-pilot).

Appendix (examples of hypothesis phrasing)
- "If we emit per-prefix cache hit rates for the top 500 prefixes, then responders will identify cache-related regressions 40% faster because they can correlate prefix drop with latency spike."
- "If we compute rolling p95 per route/model and alert on relative growth > 2x baseline, we will reduce noise from busy routes while preserving sensitivity to regressions."

Notes to self: keep scope low, prefer repeatable patterns over perfect instrumentation. Aim to produce 2 shareable observability recipes by end of Q1.
